<result>## Conclusion first

I reproduced the bug against a real workspace on disk. The loader was dropped because **its `.intropy/scaffold.json` has no `blockKind` field**, and `sys create` treats that as a *warning-level skip* (exit code 0, host still generated) rather than an error.

Evidence — `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/customers/fluxia/integrations/domains/orders/order-flow/`:

| record | `template` | `version` | `blockKind` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `order-extractor/.intropy/scaffold.json` | extractor | v0.2.1-beta.5 | `"extractor"` + `dataFlow: "in"` |
| `order-loader/.intropy/scaffold.json` | loader | v0.2.1-beta.5 | **absent** (no `dataFlow` either) |

and the generated host `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/customers/fluxia/integrations/domains/orders/order-flow/system-host/OrderFlowSystem.cs` contains only:

```csharp
    public void Define(SystemBuilder builder)
    {
        builder.AddExtractor("order-extractor").Publishes(Topics.Orders);
    }
```

Why the record lacks the field: the `blockKind`/`dataFlow` plumbing is **uncommitted** in this repo (`git diff internal/template/create.go` adds lines 124-125), while the binary on PATH is `/opt/homebrew/bin/intropy` → `intropy 0.7.0 (commit 617e875d…)`, which is exactly current `HEAD` — i.e. a binary **without** blockKind recording. The templates are innocent: `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-templates/loader/template.yaml:12-15` carries `intropy.dev/block-kind: loader` and `intropy.dev/data-flow: "out"` at the very tag that was used (`v0.2.1-beta.5` = `dd78568`), identical in shape to `extractor/template.yaml:12-15`. So the loader record was written by a binary/run that predates the label plumbing, and the extractor record by one that has it (mixed binaries, 40 s apart: 12:23:22 vs 12:24:02).

The design defect this exposes: nothing cross-checks the two records, `dataFlow` is recorded but never read, the `template` field literally says `"loader"` and is never used as a fallback, and the run exits 0 with a one-line stderr warning plus a misleading success line (`assembled system "order-flow": 1 component(s), 1 topic(s)`).

---

## 1. Discovery of components and scaffold records

- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/cmd/intropy/sys_create.go` → `cmd/intropy/sys_create.go:23-44`: cobra `sys create` calls `system.Create`.
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/system/create.go:100-110`:

```go
	entries, warnings := template.ListScaffolds(opts.StartDir)
	for _, w := range warnings {
		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "warning: %v\n", w)
	}
	model, err := Assemble(entries, func(format string, args ...any) {
		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "warning: "+format+"\n", args...)
	})
```

- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/scaffold_list.go:36-69` — `ListScaffolds` walks `root`, and for each dir containing `.intropy/scaffold.json` appends a `ScaffoldEntry` then **stops descending** (`return fs.SkipDir`, line 63). `listSkipDirs` (lines 13-19) also prunes `.git`, `.intropy`, `node_modules`, `bin`, `dist`.
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/scaffold.go:120-131` — `LoadScaffold` parses the record; `Scaffold.BlockKind` is at `scaffold.go:72` (`json:"blockKind,omitempty"`), `DataFlow` at `:76`.
- Record producers: `internal/template/create.go:116-129` (top-level `int create`) and `internal/template/dependencies.go:132-145` (dependency renders), both via `blockKindFromLabels(tmpl.Metadata.Labels)` (`scaffold.go:95-97`, label key `intropy.dev/block-kind` at `scaffold.go:39`).

## 2. How the registration code is generated

Registration is **one place only**: the generated `ISystemDefinition` class. `system-host/skeleton/Program.cs` discovers by reflection (`Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly()` → `IntropyAspire.RunAsync`), so a missing `builder.AddLoader(...)` line removes the loader from Aspire resources, `check`, `graph` and `generate` alike.

The template — `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/system/codegen.go:31-45`:

```go
const systemClassFileTmpl = `using Intropy.Topology;
...
    public void Define(SystemBuilder builder)
    {
{{- range .Components }}
        builder.{{ .Add }}("{{ .AppID }}").{{ .Edge }}(Topics.{{ .Field }});
{{- end }}
    }
}
`
```

The data — `codegen.go:72-98`. Note there is **no filtering here at all**: every `m.Components` entry gets exactly one registration line, so the drop happens upstream in `Assemble`.

```go
	for i, c := range m.Components {
		v := componentView{AppID: c.AppID, Field: fieldByKey[c.Topic]}
		if c.Kind == intropytemplate.BlockKindExtractor {
			v.Add, v.Edge = "AddExtractor", "Publishes"
		} else {
			v.Add, v.Edge = "AddLoader", "Subscribes"
		}
		views[i] = v
	}
```
(`internal/system/codegen.go:83-91`)

`writeSystemClassFile` also refuses to *create* the file (`codegen.go:73-76`) — it only overwrites the template's placeholder.

The list of components comes from `Assemble` — `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/system/assemble.go:31-49` and `:83`:

```go
	for _, e := range entries {
		switch {
		case e.Role == template.RoleSharedLibrary:
			...
			continue
		case e.Role == template.RoleSystemHost:
			warnf("skipping %s: an existing system host", e.Path)
			continue
		case e.BlockKind == "":
			warnf("skipping %s: scaffold record has no block kind — re-scaffold with a newer template release to include it", e.Path)
			continue
		case e.BlockKind != template.BlockKindExtractor && e.BlockKind != template.BlockKindLoader:
			warnf("skipping %s: unsupported block kind %q (sys create assembles extractors and loaders only)", e.Path, e.BlockKind)
			continue
		}
```

**`assemble.go:43-45` is the exact line that dropped the loader.** It is the only gate that fired; everything downstream (`Topics.cs`, csproj reference, `--output-json`) then reflected a 1-component system.

## 3. blockKind switches/maps — is "loader" handled everywhere?

There is no map keyed on blockKind anywhere; only three places branch on it:

1. `internal/system/assemble.go:46` — allow-list `{extractor, loader}`. Exact, case-sensitive string compare against `BlockKindExtractor = "extractor"` / `BlockKindLoader = "loader"` (`internal/template/scaffold.go:48-49`). Loader *is* handled; `reconciler`/`assembler` are deliberately unsupported and warn (`:47`).
2. `internal/system/codegen.go:85-89` — binary `if extractor / else loader`. The `else` is a **silent catch-all**: any kind that ever gets past the `Assemble` gate but isn't exactly `"extractor"` is emitted as `AddLoader(...).Subscribes(...)`. So a casing mismatch on the *extractor* side (`"Extractor"`) would today be rejected by `Assemble`; if that gate is ever loosened, the extractor becomes a loader silently.
3. `internal/template/{create.go:124, dependencies.go:140}` — pass-through copy of the label; no normalization (no `strings.ToLower`/`TrimSpace`). A template label of `Loader`, `LOADER`, or `loader ` would land verbatim in the record and then be skipped as "unsupported block kind" at `assemble.go:46`.

Additional silent-drop path worth flagging: the `switch` in `assemble.go:32-39` tests `Role` **before** `BlockKind`, and `RoleSharedLibrary` `continue`s with **no warning at all**. Any block template that gains a `intropy.dev/template-role` label would vanish from the system with zero output.

`dataFlow` (`"in"`/`"out"`) is recorded (`scaffold.go:76`, written at `create.go:125`) but read nowhere — grep confirms zero consumers. It is an available, unused signal for inferring/validating kind.

## 4. Topology/edge-based filtering

None. Topics are derived in the same loop that builds components (`assemble.go:73-83`), and `writeSystemClassFile` renders one edge per component with no edge/topology predicate. The only edge-adjacent risk is `fieldByKey[c.Topic]` (`codegen.go:84`): a Go map miss yields `""`, which would emit `.Subscribes(Topics.)` — uncompilable rather than dropped. Currently unreachable, because `fieldByKey` is built from the same `byTopic` map the components were keyed against.

Hard-error paths (not silent drops): duplicate `appId` (`assemble.go:68-70`), conflicting contracts on one topic key (`:74-77`), C# field-name collisions (`:111-117`), zero/multiple shared libraries (`:89-98`), missing `appId`/`topic`/`contract` values (`:51-66`).

## 5. Test coverage

- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/system/create_test.go:113-120, 168-192, 194-256` — `TestCreateAssemblesSystem` is the end-to-end registration test; the loader **is** covered on the happy path, with the exact expected line at `create_test.go:189`: `builder.AddLoader("order-loader").Subscribes(Topics.Orders);`. Note `writeBlock` (`create_test.go:122-138`) always sets `BlockKind: kind`, so the fixture can never reproduce the reported record shape.
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/system/assemble_test.go:49-78` (`TestAssembleHappyPath`), `:80-98`, `:113-207` (error table, several rows use `loaderEntry`).
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/system/assemble_test.go:216-250` (`TestAssembleSkipsWithWarnings`) — **the gap**. It exercises exactly the failing gate, but the record with no block kind is `Template: "extractor"` (`:222-224`), and the "unsupported kind" case is `"reconciler"` (`:233`). There is no test where a **loader** record lacks `blockKind`, no test that a partially-assembled system is surfaced as anything stronger than a stderr warning, and no test of a loader-only workspace or of kind-casing normalization.
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/cmd/intropy/sys_create_test.go` — flag wiring only (required `--name`, rejects `--set`); nothing about registration.
- `internal/template/dependencies_test.go` (modified, +9 lines) asserts the dependency record carries the labels; there is no equivalent assertion for the top-level `Create` path in `internal/template/create_test.go`.

Documented behaviour matching the failure: `README.md:371-373` (uncommitted) — "Records without a `blockKind` (scaffolded by an older CLI) or with a block kind other than extractor/loader are skipped with a warning."

### Fix directions this points at
- Fall back to `Scaffold.Template` and/or `DataFlow` when `BlockKind == ""` in `assemble.go:43`, or hard-error instead of warn.
- Normalize the label (`strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(...))`) in `blockKindFromLabels` (`scaffold.go:95-97`).
- Replace the `else` in `codegen.go:85-89` with an explicit `switch` on kind plus a `default:` that errors.
- Make the summary line at `create.go:162-163` report skipped records, and consider a non-zero exit or explicit `--allow-partial` when any record was skipped.
- Reorder the `Assemble` switch so a present `BlockKind` beats a stray `Role`, and warn (not silently `continue`) on the shared-library branch.</result>

Found it. The loader's scaffold record is missing the `blockKind` field, so `sys create` skipped it with a stderr warning and generated the host with only the extractor.

Here's the full chain:

**What happened in your workspace.** In `order-flow`, the two component records differ:
- `order-extractor/.intropy/scaffold.json` has `"blockKind": "extractor"` (and `dataFlow: "in"`)
- `order-loader/.intropy/scaffold.json` has **no `blockKind` at all**

`Assemble` in `internal/system/assemble.go:43-45` skips any record without a block kind — it prints `warning: skipping ...: scaffold record has no block kind — re-scaffold with a newer template release to include it` and continues, exits 0, and reports `assembled system "order-flow": 1 component(s), 1 topic(s)`. So `OrderFlowSystem.cs` ended up with only `builder.AddExtractor("order-extractor")...`, and since the host discovers definitions by reflection, the loader vanished from everything downstream.

**Why the record was missing the field.** The `blockKind`/`dataFlow` recording is part of your *uncommitted* work in `internal/template/create.go` — the released binary on your PATH (`/opt/homebrew/bin/intropy` 0.7.0, built at current HEAD, which doesn't include it) doesn't write it. The scaffold timestamps show the two components were created 40 seconds apart, evidently with different binaries: the extractor with your dev build, the loader with the Homebrew one. The loader template itself is fine — `intropy-templates/loader/template.yaml` at `v0.2.1-beta.5` carries the `intropy.dev/block-kind: loader` label just like the extractor's.

**Immediate fix for the tutorial run:** re-scaffold `order-loader` with your dev build (or add `"blockKind": "loader"` to its scaffold.json by hand), then re-run `sys create`.

The investigation also flagged some CLI weaknesses this exposed: the skip is easy to miss (warning + exit 0 + a success line that doesn't mention skips), the label value is never normalized (a `Loader` label would be rejected as "unsupported"), `codegen.go`'s extractor/else branch silently treats anything non-extractor as a loader, and there's no test for a loader record missing `blockKind`.

<result>## Root cause (confirmed)

`order-loader/.intropy/scaffold.json` is **missing the `blockKind` and `dataFlow` fields**. `intropy sys create` silently skips any scaffold record without a `blockKind`, so the loader never made it into `OrderFlowSystem.cs`. The extractor's record has both fields; the loader's does not. The two records were written by **different CLI builds** (details in section 4).

---

## 1. Directory tree

`/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/customers/fluxia/integrations/domains/orders/order-flow` (build output elided):

```
order-flow/
├── Contracts/                 (.intropy/scaffold.json, Order.cs, OrderLine.cs, Contracts.csproj)
├── order-extractor/           (.intropy/scaffold.json, src/{Program.cs,ExtractorRunner.cs,Process/*,Model/In.cs}, test/, local/, Dockerfile, Taskfile.yml)
├── order-loader/              (.intropy/scaffold.json, src/{Program.cs,LoaderRunner.cs,Process/*,Model/Out.cs}, test/, local/, Dockerfile, Taskfile.yml)
└── system-host/
    ├── .intropy/scaffold.json
    ├── OrderFlow.SystemHost.csproj
    ├── OrderFlowSystem.cs
    ├── Program.cs
    ├── Topics.cs
    ├── Properties/launchSettings.json
    ├── README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Taskfile.yml
```

Notably absent: there is **no** `order-flow/.intropy/` at the workspace root, no `match.json`, no system manifest, no generated topology/`out/` directory (those only appear after `dotnet run -- generate ./out`). The only records in the workspace are the four `.intropy/scaffold.json` files.

## 2. The registration code — the loader is missing

`/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/customers/fluxia/integrations/domains/orders/order-flow/system-host/OrderFlowSystem.cs` (whole file body):

```csharp
public sealed class OrderFlowSystem : ISystemDefinition
{
    public string SystemName => "order-flow";

    public void Define(SystemBuilder builder)
    {
        builder.AddExtractor("order-extractor").Publishes(Topics.Orders);
    }
}
```

Registered: `order-extractor` (extractor, `Publishes`).
Missing: `builder.AddLoader("order-loader").Subscribes(Topics.Orders);` — exactly the line the tutorial shows at `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/intropy-techdocs/docs/tutorials/system/03-systemhost.md:82-95`.

`Topics.cs` is complete and correct (the topic was assembled from a record, and the extractor alone defines it):

```csharp
public static readonly TopicRef<Order> Orders = TopicRef<Order>.Define("pubsub", "orders");
```

`Program.cs` contains no registration at all — it is discovery-based (`Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly()` → `IntropyAspire.RunAsync` / `IntropyGenerate.RunAsync`), so `OrderFlowSystem.Define()` is the single registration point. `OrderFlow.SystemHost.csproj` references only `../Contracts/Contracts.csproj`; components are not `ProjectReference`d, so the csproj is not implicated.

## 3. Scaffold records

**`/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/customers/fluxia/integrations/domains/orders/order-flow/order-loader/.intropy/scaffold.json` (full):**

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "template": "loader",
  "owner": "integrio-intropy",
  "repo": "intropy-templates",
  "version": "v0.2.1-beta.5",
  "values": {
    "appId": "order-loader",
    "contract": "Order",
    "contracts": "Contracts",
    "empty": false,
    "name": "OrderLoader",
    "organization": "Fluxia",
    "pubsub": "pubsub",
    "topic": "orders"
  },
  "dependsOn": [
    { "template": "shared-contracts", "dir": "../Contracts" }
  ]
}
```

**`.../order-extractor/.intropy/scaffold.json` (full, for comparison):**

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "template": "extractor",
  "owner": "integrio-intropy",
  "repo": "intropy-templates",
  "version": "v0.2.1-beta.5",
  "values": {
    "appId": "order-extractor",
    "contract": "Order",
    "contracts": "Contracts",
    "empty": false,
    "name": "OrderExtractor",
    "organization": "Fluxia",
    "pubsub": "pubsub",
    "topic": "orders"
  },
  "blockKind": "extractor",
  "dataFlow": "in",
  "dependsOn": [
    { "template": "shared-contracts", "dir": "../Contracts" }
  ]
}
```

The other two: `Contracts/.intropy/scaffold.json` has `"role": "shared-library"`, `system-host/.intropy/scaffold.json` has `"role": "system-host"` with values `name: order-flow`, `projectName: OrderFlow`, `systemClass: OrderFlowSystem`. Both correct.

## 4. What is off about the loader specifically

**Only difference: the two missing keys.** Every `values` entry is present and correctly cased (`appId: order-loader`, `contract: Order`, `topic: orders`, `pubsub: pubsub`, `name: OrderLoader`) — naming, casing, and `dependsOn` are all identical in form to the extractor. Nothing else differs.

**Why that kills registration** — `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/system/assemble.go:43`:

```go
case e.BlockKind == "":
    warnf("skipping %s: scaffold record has no block kind — re-scaffold with a newer template release to include it", e.Path)
    continue
```

The warning goes to stderr as `warning: skipping order-loader: ...` (`internal/system/create.go:104-106`) — easy to miss in the create output. `internal/system/codegen.go:85` then only emits `AddLoader`/`Subscribes` for components that survived that filter.

**Why the field is missing — not a template bug.** The label exists in the templates repo at the exact version recorded (`v0.2.1-beta.5` = commit `dd78568`, local HEAD, clean tree) — `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-templates/loader/template.yaml:12-15`:

```yaml
  labels:
    intropy.io/template-level: example
    intropy.dev/block-kind: loader
    intropy.dev/data-flow: "out"
```

The cause is **which binary wrote each record**:

| | mtime | writer |
|---|---|---|
| `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/intropy/0.7.0/intropy` (what `intropy` on PATH resolves to) | installed 11:07 | `strings` contains `intropy.dev/template-role` and `dependsOn` but **zero** hits for `intropy.dev/block-kind`, `AddLoader`, `no block kind` — this build cannot record `blockKind`/`dataFlow` and has no `sys create` codegen |
| `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/bin/intropy` (local dev build) | built 12:22 | contains `intropy.dev/block-kind`, `no block kind`, `AddLoader` |
| `order-extractor/.intropy/scaffold.json` | 12:23 | has `blockKind` → dev build |
| `order-loader/.intropy/scaffold.json` | 12:24 | no `blockKind` → Homebrew 0.7.0 |
